title: Briefing for 2026-11-02
intro: Good morning. Here is your briefing for 2026-11-02: US markets, global news, and the Philippines, in five minutes.
us: Euro zone economy slows to 0.4% growth in Q3 as crisis-hit France contracts. European Central Bank keeps key interest rate on hold at 2.5%. Third-quarter U.S. GDP increases a better-than-expected 3.4% as September inflation accelerates. The politics of President Lagarde's European Central Bank early exit — and who could replace her. Analysis: Kevin Warsh is keeping Wall Street guessing. It may be his most powerful tool. Here are five key takeaways from the Fed rate decision and Warsh news conference.
global: Ukraine air raid app apparently hacked as users receive false radiation threat, Air Force says. Israeli strikes in Gaza kill eight including child, hospitals say. France launches attempted murder investigation after petrol bomb thrown at police. University of Cambridge scientist among those who died in Spanish train crash. Armed police start patrols in Sydney after Bondi Beach attack. Shops looted as German cost-of-living protests turn violent.
philippines: House spends P100M a year on utilities. Why ask for P1B?. LIST: Flights canceled, rescheduled due to ASEAN November 2026 summit. Philip Juico, former Philippine Sports Commission chair, dies. Trump White House maps path to govern without Congress if Democrats win.
outro: That's your briefing. Have a great day.
